method.description: Actual source and all chronological contact sheets inspected using view_image. Evenly spaced frames include 0, 4 and last. CPU FFmpeg decoding, filtering and PNG encoding limited to two threads each; no GPU or generation submission. Also inspected extracted frame 56 at full resolution to assess the transient impact distortion.

observations: Compared against the exact approved replacement source: two distinct purple/yellow round-headed mallets and two short block feet replace the old malformed long support.

Both mallets remain separate head-and-handle objects throughout all 32 samples, lifting, rotating and striking the coloured bars. Their handles do not become legs, and both squat feet remain attached to the base.

The five coloured bars persist. Struck bars briefly tilt/depress; at sample 56 the yellow bar and mallet outlines soften and its lower fastener becomes indistinct, then recover in later samples. This is a localized impact-animation artifact, not a persistent missing bar or malformed support.

The xylophone remains recognizable and face-free, with readable alternating mallet motion. The complete instrument and moving mallets stay inside the frame without accumulating drift or sudden object disappearance.
limitations: Sampled still-frame inspection, not real-time playback or inspection of every frame. Motion observations describe progression across samples; frame-perfect smoothness, inter-sample artifacts and seamless looping are not guaranteed.
Contact sheets use reduced-size frames; full-resolution extracted samples are retained beside them.
scope: Exact-source and exact-video sampled visual reward-video review only. No painting processing, build, emulator, imports or integration performed or approved.
